title: Occupier's liability concerns the duty owed by a person sufficiently in control of premises to lawful visitors and, in appropriate cases, trespassers.

content.study: Occupier's liability concerns the duty owed by a person sufficiently in control of premises to lawful visitors and, in appropriate cases, trespassers.\n\nWheat v Lacon established that occupation is a question of control rather than title. Modern analysis uses reasonable care in light of visitor status, premises and foreseeable risk, supplemented by any statutory duties.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: Wheat v Lacon established that occupation is a question of control rather than title. Modern analysis uses reasonable care in light of visitor status, premises and foreseeable risk, supplemented by any statutory duties.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: No single Indian statute codifies occupiers' liability. Common-law negligence, statutory building duties and special premises legislation may apply.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Sufficient occupation or control. 2. Duty to the claimant. 3. Foreseeable risk. 4. Failure to take reasonable precautions. 5. Causation and damage.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Inspection records, maintenance logs, warning signs, photographs and CCTV may establish control, defect and foreseeability.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Plead control, visitor status, hazard, breach, causation and damage. Check special statutory regimes and limitation.
